## Partners and programs

No entry claims a partnership, endorsement, reseller right or certification. Every relationship is 'none' until a reference exists: 'applied' needs an application reference; 'member' and 'partner' need an agreement reference, scope and expiry date. Program names, tracks and requirements are volatile and expire with their sources.

## Field inventions

Field entries are published work that changed how AI systems are built. Each cites its primary record (an arXiv first version or a dated announcement) and names the catalog roles it shaped; the date is that record's date, not a claim about who was first. Our entries are contribution hypotheses: each names the files that implement it, the evidence for its present status and an experiment that could falsify it. Novelty is unassessed for every one of them; none is a patent, first-of-its-kind or proven-return claim. arXiv records were matched by identifier, title and first author against a research index on the check date.

Records checked on 2026-10-14.

| Date | Invention | Origin | Primary record | Roles it shaped | Consequence for an architect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2016-03-30 | Hierarchical navigable small-world graphs | Malkov and Yashunin | [arXiv:1603.09320](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.09320) | retrieval, store | Graph-based approximate nearest-neighbour search became the default index inside vector stores, which is what makes embedding retrieval practical at corpus scale. |
| 2017-06-12 | The Transformer | Vaswani et al. | [arXiv:1706.03762](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762) | model | Self-attention replaced recurrence, so training parallelised across sequence positions; every model the catalog routes to descends from this architecture. |
| 2018-10-11 | Bidirectional pre-trained encoders (BERT) | Devlin et al. | [arXiv:1810.04805](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04805) | model, retrieval | Pre-training an encoder once and fine-tuning it per task made pre-trained encoders the starting point for search, classification and extraction; the retrievers in this register build on them. |
| 2019-08-27 | Sentence embeddings for similarity search | Reimers and Gurevych | [arXiv:1908.10084](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084) | ingest, retrieval | Siamese training produced sentence embeddings comparable by cosine similarity, which made embedding a corpus once at ingest time and searching it by vector a practical pipeline. |
| 2020-01-23 | Neural scaling laws | Kaplan et al. | [arXiv:2001.08361](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.08361) | model | Loss was shown to fall predictably with parameters, data and compute, which turned model training into a capital-planning problem and explains why most teams buy models rather than train them. |
| 2020-04-10 | Dense passage retrieval | Karpukhin et al. | [arXiv:2004.04906](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.04906) | retrieval, ingest | Learned dual encoders retrieved passages that keyword search missed, establishing embeddings computed at ingest time as a retrieval baseline. |
| 2020-04-27 | Late-interaction retrieval (ColBERT) | Khattab and Zaharia | [arXiv:2004.12832](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.12832) | retrieval | Token-level matching after independent encoding sits between single-vector search and full cross-encoder re-ranking, and is the usual reference for multi-vector retrieval. |
| 2020-05-22 | Retrieval-augmented generation | Lewis et al. | [arXiv:2005.11401](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401) | retrieval, model | Separating what the model knows from what the corpus says made answers citable and corpora updatable without retraining; it is the basis of the catalog's cite-or-refuse contract. |
| 2020-05-28 | In-context learning at scale | Brown et al. | [arXiv:2005.14165](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165) | model, agent | Tasks could be specified with instructions and examples in the prompt instead of a fine-tuned model, which made the prompt an application artifact to version and test. |
| 2021-01-11 | Sparse mixture-of-experts at scale | Fedus et al. | [arXiv:2101.03961](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.03961) | model | Routing each token to one expert decoupled parameter count from per-token compute, so model size stopped being a reliable proxy for serving cost. |
| 2021-06-17 | Low-rank adaptation | Hu et al. | [arXiv:2106.09685](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685) | model | Training small low-rank updates on a frozen model made adapters cheap to train, store and swap per tenant or task. |
| 2022-01-28 | Chain-of-thought prompting | Wei et al. | [arXiv:2201.11903](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.11903) | agent | Asking for intermediate steps improved multi-step answers, and spending tokens on reasoning became a cost and latency decision an architect has to make explicitly. |
| 2022-03-04 | Instruction following from human feedback | Ouyang et al. | [arXiv:2203.02155](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155) | model | Fine-tuning on demonstrations and human preference rankings produced models that follow instructions, the behaviour every assistant product now assumes. |
| 2022-03-21 | Self-consistency decoding | Wang et al. | [arXiv:2203.11171](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11171) | agent, evals | Sampling several reasoning paths and taking the majority answer trades extra calls for reliability, and the agreement rate doubles as a cheap uncertainty signal. |
| 2022-05-27 | IO-aware exact attention | Dao et al. | [arXiv:2205.14135](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14135) | model | Tiling attention around GPU memory movement cut its memory footprint without approximation, which is part of why long context windows became affordable to serve. |
| 2022-10-06 | Interleaved reasoning and acting (ReAct) | Yao et al. | [arXiv:2210.03629](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629) | agent, tools | Alternating thoughts with tool calls and observations gave the agent loop its common shape: decide, act, read the result, decide again. |
| 2022-11-30 | Speculative decoding | Leviathan et al. | [arXiv:2211.17192](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192) | model | A small draft model proposes tokens that the large model verifies in parallel, lowering latency while keeping the large model's output distribution. |
| 2022-12-15 | Constitutional AI | Bai et al. | [arXiv:2212.08073](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08073) | guardrail, model | Written principles plus model-generated critiques replaced much of the human labelling for harmlessness, making a policy document part of the training input. |
| 2023-02-09 | Self-taught tool use | Schick et al. | [arXiv:2302.04761](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761) | tools | A model learned when to call an API and how to use the result, framing tools as something a model chooses rather than something a pipeline forces. |
| 2023-02-23 | Indirect prompt injection | Greshake et al. | [arXiv:2302.12173](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.12173) | guardrail, tools, retrieval | Instructions hidden in retrieved or tool-returned content can steer the model, so every retrieved document and tool result is untrusted input and tool authority must be bounded outside the model. |
| 2023-03-20 | Verbal self-reflection (Reflexion) | Shinn et al. | [arXiv:2303.11366](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366) | agent, memory | Agents that write down why an attempt failed and read it on the next attempt improve without weight updates, which makes episodic memory a design element. |
| 2023-05-17 | Tree of thoughts | Yao et al. | [arXiv:2305.10601](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10601) | orchestrator, agent | Exploring and pruning several partial solutions turns reasoning into a search an orchestrator can budget, with an explicit trade between calls and quality. |
| 2023-05-23 | Quantized low-rank adaptation | Dettmers et al. | [arXiv:2305.14314](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14314) | model | Training adapters on a quantized base model brought fine-tuning of large open models within reach of a single accelerator. |
| 2023-05-29 | Direct preference optimization | Rafailov et al. | [arXiv:2305.18290](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18290) | model | Preference tuning without a separate reward model or reinforcement-learning loop made it a supervised training job that more teams can run. |
| 2023-06-09 | Model-graded evaluation | Zheng et al. | [arXiv:2306.05685](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685) | evals | Strong models agree with human preference often enough to grade open-ended output, and they carry measurable position and verbosity biases, so a judge is itself something to calibrate. |
| 2023-06-13 | Function calling in a model API | OpenAI | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/function-calling-and-other-api-updates) | tools, api | Models emitted structured calls against developer-declared schemas, moving tool use from prompt parsing into the API contract. |
| 2023-07-06 | Position sensitivity in long context | Liu et al. | [arXiv:2307.03172](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172) | retrieval, memory | Models used information at the start and end of a long context more reliably than the middle, so the order and size of retrieved context are design parameters, not details. |
| 2023-09-12 | Paged attention for serving (vLLM) | Kwon et al. | [arXiv:2309.06180](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180) | model | Managing the attention cache in pages, like virtual memory, let servers batch far more concurrent requests and set the template for open-source model serving. |
| 2023-09-26 | Reference-free retrieval evaluation (Ragas) | Es et al. | [arXiv:2309.15217](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15217) | evals, retrieval | Faithfulness, answer relevance and context relevance became separate metrics, so a failing retrieval system can be traced to the retriever or the generator. |
| 2024-04-24 | Graph-based retrieval over community summaries | Edge et al. | [arXiv:2404.16130](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16130) | retrieval, ingest | Building an entity graph and summarising its communities at ingest time answers corpus-wide questions that chunk retrieval cannot, at the cost of a heavier ingest pipeline. |
| 2024-08-06 | Schema-constrained output | OpenAI | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/introducing-structured-outputs-in-the-api/) | api, guardrail | Constraining generation to a supplied JSON Schema turned output validation from a retry loop into a guarantee of the decoding step. |
| 2024-11-25 | Model Context Protocol | Anthropic; donated to the Agentic AI Foundation | [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-context-protocol) | tools, gateway | One open protocol for exposing tools, resources and prompts to any model client replaced per-integration adapters; it underlies the catalog's tool hub pattern. |
| 2025-04-09 | Agent2Agent protocol | Google; moved to the Linux Foundation | [Google for Developers Blog](https://developers.googleblog.com/en/a2a-a-new-era-of-agent-interoperability/) | orchestrator, agent | Agents built on different frameworks can discover each other's capabilities and exchange tasks, the agent-to-agent counterpart to MCP's agent-to-tool interface. |

## Proposed original contributions

| ID | Contribution | Mechanism | Status | Implemented in | Evidence | Experiment that could falsify it | Prior work to check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I01 | Experience-to-topology compiler | One pattern file holds the customer journey, component IDs and flows; the compiler emits React Flow, Mermaid, diagrams.net, SVG and Structurizr views that share those IDs, so no view is drawn by hand. | Implemented | `catalog/compile.mjs`, `catalog/compile.test.mjs` | Tests assert identical component and flow IDs across views and byte-identical output for identical input. | Give two teams the same change request, one editing hand-drawn views and one editing the pattern file; compare drift between views and time to a consistent set. | Architecture-as-code tools, the C4 model and Structurizr, model-driven engineering. |
| I02 | Evidence-preserving portal | Every maturity the portal displays must be backed by an artifact-specific receipt; the compiler refuses to promote a fixture beyond 'visualized' or import runtime receipts. | Partial | `solution-kit/compile.mjs`, `solution-kit/portal.html` | The compiler rejects runtime maturity and receipts in fixtures. No live receipt has been recorded, so promotion with real evidence is untested. | Hand a reviewer contradictory receipts and measure how often a higher maturity is displayed than the receipts support. | Software supply-chain provenance (SLSA, in-toto), evidence-based assessment. |
| I03 | Dual value ledger | Customer value counts only accepted results, while cost counts every attempt; the provider's consumption drivers are shown beside it and never move the customer score. | Partial | `catalog/compile.mjs`, `catalog/providers.json` | The economics function and its test charge failed attempts. The figures are assumptions per pattern; no pilot data exists. | Run one pilot with the ledger and one without; compare whether scope decisions improve net customer value without consumption that buys no accepted result. | Unit economics, FinOps cost allocation, value-stream measurement. |
| I04 | Source-drift gate | Every product and program claim carries a checked-on and review-by date; the compiler stops when one passes, so stale claims cannot be published. | Partial | `catalog/compile.mjs`, `catalog/sources.json` | A test proves compilation fails on an expired source. The gate does not yet list which pages, templates or chapters depend on the expired claim. | Expire one API claim and measure how many dependent artifacts a maintainer finds with and without a generated dependency list. | Documentation linting, dependency freshness bots, citation management. |
| I05 | Portable acceptance capsule | Tests, results, ownership and rollback steps are exported with the solution so a customer can re-run acceptance on their own host. | Partial | `solution-kit/practice.mjs`, `solution-kit/practice.test.mjs` | The practice domain runs against a synthetic fixture only; no customer host has reproduced a capsule. | Reproduce one capsule on a fresh customer host and record every manual step needed. | Reproducible builds, acceptance-test-driven development, release evidence packs. |
| I06 | Industry R&D workbench | Evidence-linked industry cases generate solution variants and lab missions from the same catalog. | Proposed | Nothing yet | Described in this register only; nothing runs. | Compare time to a reviewable design against an existing discovery workflow on the same brief. | Design-space exploration tools, pattern languages, case-based reasoning. |
| I07 | One answer contract on three runtimes | A single cite-or-refuse contract module is copied verbatim into the Vercel, Cloudflare and Cloud Run templates, and one conformance suite runs against all three. | Implemented | `templates/deploy/answer-core/answer-core.mjs`, `templates/deploy/answer-core/sync.mjs`, `templates/deploy/answer-core/conformance.test.mjs` | The sync check fails when a template's copy drifts, and conformance tests run locally. No provider deployment receipt exists. | Deploy all three and run the conformance suite against each live endpoint; record any behaviour that differs by runtime. | Consumer-driven contract testing, OpenAPI conformance suites. |
| I08 | Reweightable judgement scorecard | Each realization carries a recorded 1-to-5 judgement per criterion with a written rationale, published per criterion so a reader can reweight them; no score is presented as a benchmark, and provider consumption never changes a customer score. | Implemented | `catalog/providers.json`, `catalog/patterns` | Validation rejects scores outside 1 to 5 and realizations without a rationale. | Ask several architects to score the same realizations independently and measure agreement before publishing a ranking. | Multi-criteria decision analysis, architecture trade-off analysis (ATAM). |
| I09 | Verified-icon rule | Official vendor icons are embedded only from a hash-pinned registry and only for that vendor's services; every other node uses a neutral role glyph. | Implemented | `catalog/compile.mjs`, `solution-kit/icons/registry.json` | The compiler fails on a hash mismatch or on an official icon attached to another provider's service; a test covers the second. | Audit a sample of generated diagrams against vendor icon terms and count misattributed marks. | Vendor icon kits and their usage terms, asset provenance in design systems. |
| I10 | Name-evidence ledger | Every service name carries how it was verified (a registered source, a long-standing name, or inferred from a rename); inferred or non-GA names are flagged to confirm before customer use. | Implemented | `catalog/services.json`, `catalog/compile.mjs` | Validation requires registered sources for source-verified names, and each realization lists the bindings to confirm. | Re-check flagged and unflagged names against vendor documentation and compare the error rate of each group. | Data lineage and provenance tagging. |

Novelty is unassessed for every contribution. Check the prior work named in each row before calling any of them new.
